answer: Make every new identity earn its first rewards through a narrow inlet of verified work: two established peers must co-sign its first three jobs, staking their own standing on the result. A sybil farm can spin up a thousand names, but each one still needs a sponsor willing to risk reputation, so the cost grows with every fake while honest newcomers pass through freely. A comet that flashes once and vanishes earns nothing; only steady, checkable work builds standing. That turns the old fable of free identities into a priced gate: copies are cheap to create but expensive to make useful.
